user_query: How does the optimal dimensionality of DeepWalk depend on the amount of training data available in the Flickr and BlogCatalog experiments?
llm_response: In the Flickr and BlogCatalog experiments, the best-performing embedding dimensionality increases as more training data is available. With less training data, smaller dimensions tend to work better because higher-dimensional embeddings overfit; as the amount of training data grows, larger dimensions become beneficial and the optimal dimensionality shifts upward. In other words, the experiments show a positive relationship between available training data and the dimensionality that gives the best DeepWalk performance.
llm_confidence_reasoning: This is consistent with the reported trend in the DeepWalk experiments, but I am not fully certain of the exact dataset-specific numeric optima without the original figures.
extracted_response_entities: positive relationship with best DeepWalk dimensionality

extracted_response_triples.target: positive relationship with best DeepWalk dimensionality
